cases.evidence_note: Predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: single, Form W-2 wages $215,300 (withholding $21,530) and no other income; the filer is a debtor in a chapter 11 case filed in March 2025 and still open at the end of the year. i1040gi p. 23, Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Cases: "If you are a debtor in a chapter 11 bankruptcy case, income taxable to the bankruptcy estate and reported on the estate’s income tax return includes: Earnings from services you performed after the beginning of the case (both wages and self-employment income)" and "you (or the trustee if one is appointed) must allocate between you and the bankruptcy estate the wages, salary, or other compensation and withheld income tax reported to you on Form W-2." Part of the wages and withholding belongs on the bankruptcy estate's return, an allocation (Notice 2006-83) this tool does not make, so the filer answers Yes to the other-income screen and the return is refused.

cases.evidence_note: Predicted from the archived i1040gi before evaluating: married filing jointly, the taxpayer's Form W-2 wages $120,000 and $1,500 of bank interest; the spouse, who has no income of their own, is a debtor in a chapter 11 case filed in 2024 and open throughout 2025. i1040gi p. 23, Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Cases: "If you are a debtor in a chapter 11 bankruptcy case, income taxable to the bankruptcy estate and reported on the estate’s income tax return includes: Earnings from services you performed after the beginning of the case (both wages and self-employment income)" and "you (or the trustee if one is appointed) must allocate between you and the bankruptcy estate the wages, salary, or other compensation and withheld income tax reported to you on Form W-2." Income from property described in section 541 of title 11 that the debtor owned when the case began or acquired before it closed is also the estate's, so part of the joint return's income may belong on the estate's return; the filers answer Yes to the other-income screen and the return is refused.
